items.title: Behind the push to harmonize nature frameworks
items.summary: The recent synchronization of nature frameworks and metrics is a welcome development for companies that have found it challenging to develop nature and biodiversity targets.

items.title: Hyperscaler emissions expected to jump 60 percent in 2026
items.summary: The emissions of five of the largest hyperscalers will grow by almost 60 percent this calendar year, according to the first application of a new method for forecasting corporate carbon footprints.

items.title: Study: New coal projects outpace cancellations 3 to 1
items.summary: According to new data from Urgewald, for every coal project that got cancelled last year, another three new ones were announced.

items.title: COP31 Action Tracker: Pre-COP outcomes and nature action
items.summary: With COP31 in Türkiye happening next month, this regular members-only series from edie will provide a temperature check on global climate action, including news from businesses, governments and other key organisations ahead of the summit.

items.title: TODAY: How the UK CBAM will affect sustainability strategies
items.summary: Join edie on 20th October for our 45-minute masterclass to explore what the UK CBAM means for sustainability strategies and how businesses can prepare.

items.title: UK publishes CBAM default emissions values ahead of 2027 launch
items.summary: The UK Government has published default emissions values for its Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), giving importers a standard basis for calculating potential carbon tax liabilities ahead of the scheme’s launch on 1 January 2027.

items.title: Jackdaw decision looms as clean energy investment case stacks up
items.summary: With a decision on Jackdaw gasfield expected this week, think tank E3G has warned that further North Sea drilling represents a "bad deal" for the UK and the country should instead prioritise heat pumps and insulation.

items.title: edie Energy & Tech Awards 2026 – Meet the Winners
items.summary: The winners of edie’s first Energy & Tech Awards were announced on Friday 16 October at a ceremony in central London.

items.title: Making heavy weather of economic growth: Why the UK must get serious about climate adaptation
items.summary: Climate change is presenting growing risks to our economy, but adapting to extreme weather offers opportunities too, argues Aldersgate Group policy officer, Adam Young.

items.title: What’s driving the cost of EV charging?
items.summary: Two electric vehicle charging operations can face very different costs, even though they are buying their power from the same market.
